tools.name: create_animation
tools.title: Create Animation
tools.description: Creates and selects an undoable animation with linear keyframes for existing bones, using Blockbench editor coordinates. Returns its UUID and actual name.

name.description: Animation name; `animation.` is added unless the name already starts with it, as in Bedrock and GeckoLib animation files.

animation_length.description: Length of the animation in seconds

bones.description: Keyframes keyed by existing bone/group name. Values use Blockbench editor coordinates; rotations are degrees.

additionalProperties.description: Effect name; a particle effect loaded with create_particle_effect is attached so Blockbench previews it

particle_effects.description: Particle effects with timestamps (seconds) as keys, spawned at the entity origin. Use manage_particle_keyframes for locators, scripts and more options.

tools.name: manage_keyframes
tools.title: Manage Keyframes
tools.description: Creates, deletes, or edits keyframes in the animation timeline for specific bones and channels.

animation_id.description: Animation UUID or name. If not provided, uses current animation.

bone_name.description: Name of the bone/group to manage keyframes for.

time.description: Time in seconds for the keyframe.

values.description: Values: [x,y,z] for position/rotation, number for uniform scale.

interpolation.description: Interpolation type for the keyframe. New keyframes default to linear; edits keep the current interpolation when omitted.

bezier_handles.description: Bezier handle positions for bezier interpolation.

tools.name: animation_graph_editor
tools.title: Animation Graph Editor
tools.description: Edits a bone channel's interpolation or numeric Bezier easing in one reversible edit. Uses native per-axis handle arrays and chronological segment durations. Custom points are normalized time/value fractions. Partial-axis edits require existing Bezier keys; key-wide mode changes require all axes. Rejects curve edits ignored by quaternion rotation, and step or Bezier curves in GeckoLib models (use geckolib_set_keyframe_easing). Inspect neighboring segments after range edits.

animation_id.description: Animation UUID or name. If not provided, uses current animation.

bone_name.description: Name of the bone/group to modify curves for.

axis.description: Axes to edit. Linear, stepped and smooth require all because interpolation is key-wide. Partial-axis easing/custom edits require selected keys already using Bezier interpolation, preserving other axes' handles.

action.description: Curve modification. linear, stepped and smooth set the key-wide interpolation (linear, step, catmullrom). ease_in, ease_out and ease_in_out apply the CSS cubic-bezier curves of the same name to every segment between the selected keys; custom applies custom_curve. Easing/custom require at least two distinct chronological numeric single-data-point keys. Smooth and Bezier rotation edits are unavailable when native quaternion interpolation would ignore them. GeckoLib models reject stepped (the GeckoLib plugin switches step keys back to linear) and the Bezier actions (GeckoLib has no Bezier interpolation); use geckolib_set_keyframe_easing there. In GeckoLib models smooth also clears the easings of the keys it changes, since GeckoLib ignores easings on catmullrom keys.

keyframe_range.description: Finite ordered time range selecting existing keys; omitted means the full channel. Key-wide interpolation can affect neighboring segments at range boundaries, so edit the full channel when boundary continuity matters.

control_point_1.description: Outgoing normalized control point [time fraction in 0..1, value fraction] for each selected adjacent-key segment. Finite value fractions outside 0..1 allow overshoot.

control_point_2.description: Incoming normalized control point [time fraction in 0..1, value fraction], measured from the segment start. Converted to native per-axis offsets relative to the ending key.

custom_curve.description: Normalized cubic Bezier control points, required for custom action. Conversion uses each segment's duration and edited-axis endpoint values; unrelated axis handles are preserved.

tools.name: bone_rigging
tools.title: Bone Rigging
tools.description: Creates and manipulates the bone structure (rig) of a model for animation. Each action is one undoable edit (create with ik_enabled records the IK controller as a second one); undoing delete brings back child bones, elements and their keyframes. mirror duplicates the bone with its descendants and flips the copy like Blockbench's Flip action. The set_ik action is deprecated; use set_ik_controller for Blockbench's null-object IK (source, target, pole).

action.description: Action to perform on the bone structure.

parent.description: Parent bone UUID or name; omit it or pass root for the project root (for the parent action, a bone actually named root takes precedence). An unknown parent, or a name several bones share, is an error.

children.description: Names or UUIDs of existing elements/groups to add when creating a bone. For rename, the first entry is the new name.

ik_enabled.description: Deprecated; prefer set_ik_controller. true makes this bone the end effector of a null-object IK controller (created as <bone>_ik when ik_target is omitted); false clears ik_target on controllers driving it. With create, the IK controller is a second undo entry after the bone's.

ik_target.description: Name or UUID of the null object that drives this bone as the IK controller.

mirror_axis.description: Axis the mirror action flips across (default x): the bone is duplicated with its descendants and the copy is flipped like Blockbench's Flip action, through the model origin, swapping left/right names when free.

tools.name: animation_timeline
tools.title: Animation Timeline
tools.description: Controls the animation timeline: playback, time scrubbing, length, FPS, loop mode, and keyframe selection by time range or relative to the playhead (select_before_playhead/select_after_playhead return the selected keyframe UUIDs).

animation_id.description: Animation UUID or name. If not provided, uses current animation.

action.description: Timeline action to perform. select_before_playhead/select_after_playhead replace the keyframe selection with bone keyframes at or before/after the playhead (1e-5 s tolerance, like Blockbench 5.2's native actions) and return their UUIDs.

time.description: Time in seconds. Required for set_time; for select_before_playhead/select_after_playhead it is the reference time and defaults to the current playhead.

length.description: Animation length in seconds, including all keyframes (for set_length action).

fps.description: Integer frames per second, 10–120 (for set_fps action; Blockbench minimum is 10).

scope.description: Keyframes considered by select_before_playhead/select_after_playhead. animation: every bone animator of the target animation, including ones hidden from the timeline. timeline: only animators shown in the timeline with visible channels, matching the native action; requires the target animation to be selected.

tools.name: batch_keyframe_operations
tools.title: Batch Keyframe Operations
tools.description: Edits keyframes in the active animation atomically; all includes hidden animators. Numeric value edits use native transform values. Reverse follows the native Reverse Keyframes action, including the GeckoLib plugin's easing adjustment. Bake samples continuous numeric curves within selected channel spans, caps output at 10000 samples, and restores the playhead. Expressions, step/pre-post curves and effect channels require native baking. Smooth and bake clear GeckoLib easings they replace and report it.

selection.description: Which active-animation keyframes to operate on. all includes hidden or collapsed animators.

operation.description: Operation to perform on keyframes. reverse works like Blockbench's Reverse Keyframes action: times flip within the selection, pre/post values and Bezier handles swap, and GeckoLib easings flip direction and move to the key their segment now arrives at, as the GeckoLib plugin does. smooth and bake clear the GeckoLib easings they replace and report it.

offset_time.description: Time offset to apply; resulting keyframes must remain between 0 and 10000 seconds.

offset_values.description: Numeric [x,y,z] value offset. Requires transform keyframes with a single numeric data point; expressions and pre/post values require native tools.

scale_factor.description: Scale factor for keyframe times around scale_pivot. Does not scale values; zero is accepted only when it creates no timestamp collisions. A negative factor also reverses the keys like reverse.

mirror_axis.description: Numeric component to negate. Requires transform keyframes with a single numeric data point.

bake_interval.description: Sampling interval in seconds (minimum 0.001; at most 10000 samples). Bakes only selected transform channels between their selected times. Requires continuous numeric single-data-point keyframes; expressions, effects and stepped/pre-post curves require native baking.

tools.name: animation_copy_paste
tools.title: Animation Copy/Paste
tools.description: Copies native keyframe data points and curve metadata into a plugin-local clipboard. Paste preserves exact timestamps, replaces same-channel/time collisions and is undoable, including newly created animators. Mirror paste uses native position/rotation/curve mirroring; scale is unchanged.

time_range.description: Time range to copy. If not provided, copies all keyframes.

time_offset.description: Offset for exact, unsnapped pasted timestamps; results must remain between 0 and 10000 seconds. Existing keys at the same channel/time are replaced.

mirror_axis.description: Native mirror axis for mirror_paste (default x). Position negates this axis, rotation negates the other two axes, scale is unchanged; curve handles follow native mirroring.

tools.name: variable_placeholders
tools.title: Variable Placeholders
tools.description: Reads or edits the project's animation Variable Placeholders text (one `variable = expression` per line), used to preview Molang animations. add writes a value, slider('name', step, min, max), toggle('name') or impulse('name', duration) line like the native Create Variable Placeholder dialog; set replaces all text; remove deletes a variable's lines. Changes sync through the native panel, refresh the animation preview and return the parsed lines and live controls. Placeholder edits are not recorded in Undo. Requires a format with Molang enabled.

action.description: get: read text, parsed lines and live controls. set: replace the whole text. add: write one structured line. remove: delete every line assigning variable.

text.description: Complete placeholder text for set; one `variable = expression` per line. Empty clears all placeholders.

variable.description: Variable assigned by the line, e.g. variable.speed (v./q./t./c. short prefixes are expanded by Blockbench).

value.description: Constant number or single-line Molang expression.

variable.description: Variable assigned by the line, e.g. variable.speed (v./q./t./c. short prefixes are expanded by Blockbench).

name.description: Label of the preview control shown in the Variable Placeholders panel.

step.description: Slider step; defaults to 1 when a range is given.

initial_value.description: Initial control value (toggle: 0 or 1). Preview-only; not saved as text.

variable.description: Variable assigned by the line, e.g. variable.speed (v./q./t./c. short prefixes are expanded by Blockbench).

name.description: Label of the preview control shown in the Variable Placeholders panel.

initial_value.description: Initial control value (toggle: 0 or 1). Preview-only; not saved as text.

variable.description: Variable assigned by the line, e.g. variable.speed (v./q./t./c. short prefixes are expanded by Blockbench).

name.description: Label of the preview control shown in the Variable Placeholders panel.

duration.description: Seconds the impulse stays at 1 (Blockbench default 0.1).

replace_existing.description: For add: replace an existing line for the same variable (aliases such as v. match) instead of appending a duplicate.

tools.name: list_molang_variables
tools.title: List Molang Variables
tools.description: Lists Blockbench's built-in Molang variables and query functions available in animation previews (like the native View Built-in Variables dialog), with current values for constants and live queries, plus the project's placeholder assignments. Read-only.

filter.description: Case-insensitive substring filter on variable names, e.g. 'camera'.

tools.name: set_ik_controller
tools.title: Set IK Controller
tools.description: Creates or updates an inverse-kinematics controller. Blockbench drives IK from a null object: ik_target is the end effector (group/bone, armature bone, or locator) that reaches for the null object, ik_source is the chain root (defaults to the null object's parent), ik_pole (Blockbench 5.2+) sets the bend direction, and lock_ik_target_rotation keeps the effector's rotation. Works with bone rigs and armatures (5.2 allows null objects under armatures and armature bones). Validates every reference and that the target lies below the chain root; returns the solved chain. Replaces the deprecated bone_rigging set_ik flags, which Blockbench never read.

null_object.description: UUID or name of an existing null object to update. Omit to create a new IK controller null object.

name.description: Name for the null object. Defaults to '<ik_target name>_ik' when creating.

position.description: Null object position [x, y, z] as Blockbench stores it (model space for root and group parents). Defaults to the end effector's world pivot when creating.

parent.description: Parent group, armature, or armature bone (UUID or name), or 'root'. Defaults to root when creating. When ik_source is empty the parent is the implicit chain root, so keep IK controllers outside the chain they drive.

ik_target.description: End effector that reaches for the null object: a group/bone, armature bone, or locator (UUID or name). Required when creating; must be a descendant of the chain root. Empty string clears.

ik_source.description: Chain root: a group/bone or armature bone (UUID or name). The chain spans from here down to ik_target. Empty string clears, making the null object's parent the chain root.

ik_pole.description: Pole target controlling the bend direction (Blockbench 5.2+): a group, locator, or other null object (UUID or name). Empty string clears.

lock_ik_target_rotation.description: Keep the end effector's world rotation while the chain solves.

tools.name: capture_screenshot
tools.title: Capture Screenshot
tools.description: Returns the rendered image of a view. Defaults to the user's active viewport ("active"); pass the ID of an offscreen view from create_offscreen_view to render without disturbing the user, or a viewport ID from list_views.

view.description: View to target: "active" for the viewport the user last interacted with, the ID of an offscreen view from create_offscreen_view, or a viewport ID from list_views.

max_size.description: Longest side of the returned image in pixels; larger images are scaled down proportionally. Omit for full size.

format.description: Encoding of the returned image: "png" (default, lossless), or the smaller "jpeg" (no transparency: transparent pixels become white) or "webp".

tools.name: capture_app_screenshot
tools.title: Capture App Screenshot
tools.description: Returns the image data of the Blockbench app.

max_size.description: Longest side of the returned image in pixels; larger images are scaled down proportionally. Omit for full size.

format.description: Encoding of the returned image: "png" (default, lossless), or the smaller "jpeg" (no transparency: transparent pixels become white) or "webp".

tools.name: set_camera_angle
tools.title: Set Camera Angle
tools.description: Moves a view's camera and returns the resulting frame plus the applied camera state. Defaults to the user's active viewport, which changes what they see and clears any side-view lock they had; target an offscreen view from create_offscreen_view to inspect the model from any angle without moving their camera.

view.description: View to target: "active" for the viewport the user last interacted with, the ID of an offscreen view from create_offscreen_view, or a viewport ID from list_views.

zoom.description: Orthographic zoom factor (Blockbench default 0.5). Ignored for perspective views and while a side view is locked.

fov.description: Perspective field of view in degrees. Uses the Blockbench setting when omitted.

locked_angle.description: Lock an orthographic side view (top, bottom, north, south, east, west). Omit to leave the view free.

max_size.description: Longest side of the returned image in pixels; larger images are scaled down proportionally. Omit for full size.

format.description: Encoding of the returned image: "png" (default, lossless), or the smaller "jpeg" (no transparency: transparent pixels become white) or "webp".

tools.name: create_offscreen_view
tools.title: Create Offscreen View
tools.description: Creates a private offscreen viewport that renders the current project without moving the user's camera. Use it with set_camera_angle and capture_screenshot (view: <id>) for multi-angle inspection. The camera starts where the user's is unless copy_view is "none". Up to 4 views may exist at once; delete them with delete_offscreen_view when done. Views still open when your MCP session ends are deleted.

id.description: ID for the new view. Generated as view_N when omitted.

antialias.description: Multisample antialiasing. Disable for crisp pixel-art inspection.

anyOf.description: View to target: "active" for the viewport the user last interacted with, the ID of an offscreen view from create_offscreen_view, or a viewport ID from list_views.

copy_view.description: View whose camera seeds the new one. Defaults to "active" (the user's viewport); pass "none" for Blockbench's default angle.

tools.name: list_views
tools.title: List Views
tools.description: Lists render targets: the user's connected viewports (the active one flagged) and the plugin's offscreen views, each with size and camera position, target, projection, FOV, zoom, and side-view lock.

tools.name: resize_offscreen_view
tools.title: Resize Offscreen View
tools.description: Changes the pixel size of an offscreen view. The user's viewports follow their layout and cannot be resized here.

view.description: ID of the offscreen view to resize.

tools.name: delete_offscreen_view
tools.title: Delete Offscreen View
tools.description: Disposes an offscreen view and releases its WebGL context. The user's viewports are not affected.

view.description: ID of the offscreen view to dispose.

tools.name: get_capabilities
tools.title: Get Capabilities
tools.description: Discover Blockbench/plugin versions, desktop or web environment, active project summary, and registered model formats. Returns detailed boolean format features (null means unknown; includes molang and java_cube_shade_direction_override) plus the format's remember_files and animation_grouping settings, compact supported-feature lists for all formats, and optional tool registration states. Works with no open project. Format features do not guarantee that every enabled MCP tool can run in the current mode or selection.

format_id.description: Optional registered format ID to inspect, such as 'free'. Defaults to the active project's format. Does not switch or create a project.

include_tools.description: Include all registered MCP tool names, stability status, and current enabled state. Use list_modes and set_mode to navigate before calling mode-dependent tools.

tools.name: place_cube
tools.title: Place Cube
tools.description: Creates cubes in one reversible edit. Texture and group are optional, allowing untextured blockouts. Explicit face targets never use the current UV selection; partial/custom faces require per-face UV support. Elements accept inflate, plus uv_offset and mirror_uv for box UV cubes; unknown element fields are rejected. Cubes the format's size limiter rejects (for example Java Block elements outside -16…32) are refused and nothing is created, unless Blockbench's Deactivate Size Limit setting is on.

inflate.description: Grows the cube by this amount on every side without changing from/to.

uv_offset.description: Box UV net offset [u, v]. Requires box UV.

mirror_uv.description: Mirror the box UV net. Requires box UV; for per-face mirroring, reverse the face rectangle endpoints.

shade.description: Whether to apply shading to the cube. Java 26.3+ projects ignore this flag; shade=false is mapped to shade_direction_override 'up' there, matching Blockbench's own import.

shade_direction_override.description: Java Edition 26.3+ shade direction override: the face direction whose lighting shade is applied to every face. '' removes the override. Replaces the boolean shade flag in formats with java_cube_shade_direction_override (new Java Block projects default to 26.3).

light_emission.description: Block light emitted by the cube (0-15). Exported by Java Block formats.

elements.description: Array of cubes to place, with optional Java shading fields.

texture.description: Texture UUID, ID or name. When omitted, uses the default texture if one exists; otherwise creates untextured cubes.

group.description: Parent group UUID or unique name, or root (default). Missing or ambiguous names are rejected.

anyOf.description: Array of faces to apply the texture to.
true applies texture to all faces with Auto UV; false skips texture assignment and disables Auto UV except in Hytale, which requires Auto UV 1.

face.description: Face to apply the texture to.

uv.description: Custom UV rectangle. Hytale requires absolute width/height to match the cube's face dimensions: north/south XY, east/west ZY, up/down XZ.

anyOf.description: Array of faces with custom UV mapping.

faces.description: true applies texture to all faces with Auto UV; false skips texture assignment. Named faces use Auto UV; false/custom rectangles disable Auto UV outside Hytale. Hytale always retains Auto UV 1 and custom rectangles must match the geometry's face dimensions. Partial/custom faces require per-face UV support. Single-texture formats may still display the project texture.

tools.name: modify_cube
tools.title: Modify Cube
tools.description: Modifies the cube with the given ID. Auto UV setting: saved as an integer, where 0 means disabled, 1 means enabled, and 2 means relative auto UV (cube position affects UV). A new from/to/inflate that the format's size limiter rejects (for example Java Block elements outside -16…32) is refused before anything changes, unless Blockbench's Deactivate Size Limit setting is on.

id.description: ID or name of the cube to modify. Defaults to selected, which could be more than one.

autouv.description: Auto UV setting. 0 = disabled, 1 = enabled, 2 = relative auto UV.

shade.description: Whether to apply shading to the cube. Java 26.3+ projects ignore this flag; shade=false is mapped to shade_direction_override 'up' there, matching Blockbench's own import.

shade_direction_override.description: Java Edition 26.3+ shade direction override: the face direction whose lighting shade is applied to every face. '' removes the override. Replaces the boolean shade flag in formats with java_cube_shade_direction_override (new Java Block projects default to 26.3).

light_emission.description: Block light emitted by the cube (0-15). Exported by Java Block formats.

color.description: Single digit to represent a color from a palette.

visibility.description: Whether the cube is visible or not.

tools.name: get_cube_uv
tools.title: Get Cube UV
tools.description: Inspect a cube's UV mode, offset, mirroring, six face rectangles/rotations, stored and effective texture references, logical UV sizes and bitmap sizes. Read-only; no selection or preview changes.

id.description: Cube UUID or unique name. UUID takes precedence over names.

tools.name: set_cube_uv
tools.title: Set Cube UV
tools.description: Edit box UV offsets/mirroring or per-face rectangles, rotation and texture references in one reversible edit. Preserves untargeted faces and selection. Validates UV mode, texture references and rotation support. Hytale rectangles must retain geometry-linked extents and Auto UV; texture assignments use the project/attachment collection, and quads cannot use box UV. Does not pack islands or repaint textures.

id.description: Cube UUID or unique name. Does not use or change selection.

box_uv.description: Explicitly convert UV mode using the native cube operation. Requires optional_box_uv to change mode. Conversion can reset rotations and enable disabled faces.

uv_offset.description: Box UV net offset [u, v]; requires box UV mode.

mirror_uv.description: Mirror the box UV net; requires box UV mode. For per-face mirroring, reverse rectangle endpoints.

uv.description: [u1, v1, u2, v2] in logical UV units, not necessarily bitmap pixels. Reversed and out-of-bounds rectangles are preserved. Hytale requires extents matching cube face dimensions, swapped for 90/270-degree rotation; offsets and mirroring are supported.

rotation.description: UV rotation in degrees; nonzero rotation requires format uv_rotation support.

texture.description: Texture UUID, ID or unique name; false unassigns, null disables the face. Omit to preserve.

uv.description: [u1, v1, u2, v2] in logical UV units, not necessarily bitmap pixels. Reversed and out-of-bounds rectangles are preserved. Hytale requires extents matching cube face dimensions, swapped for 90/270-degree rotation; offsets and mirroring are supported.

rotation.description: UV rotation in degrees; nonzero rotation requires format uv_rotation support.

texture.description: Texture UUID, ID or unique name; false unassigns, null disables the face. Omit to preserve.

uv.description: [u1, v1, u2, v2] in logical UV units, not necessarily bitmap pixels. Reversed and out-of-bounds rectangles are preserved. Hytale requires extents matching cube face dimensions, swapped for 90/270-degree rotation; offsets and mirroring are supported.

rotation.description: UV rotation in degrees; nonzero rotation requires format uv_rotation support.

texture.description: Texture UUID, ID or unique name; false unassigns, null disables the face. Omit to preserve.

uv.description: [u1, v1, u2, v2] in logical UV units, not necessarily bitmap pixels. Reversed and out-of-bounds rectangles are preserved. Hytale requires extents matching cube face dimensions, swapped for 90/270-degree rotation; offsets and mirroring are supported.

rotation.description: UV rotation in degrees; nonzero rotation requires format uv_rotation support.

texture.description: Texture UUID, ID or unique name; false unassigns, null disables the face. Omit to preserve.

uv.description: [u1, v1, u2, v2] in logical UV units, not necessarily bitmap pixels. Reversed and out-of-bounds rectangles are preserved. Hytale requires extents matching cube face dimensions, swapped for 90/270-degree rotation; offsets and mirroring are supported.

rotation.description: UV rotation in degrees; nonzero rotation requires format uv_rotation support.

texture.description: Texture UUID, ID or unique name; false unassigns, null disables the face. Omit to preserve.

uv.description: [u1, v1, u2, v2] in logical UV units, not necessarily bitmap pixels. Reversed and out-of-bounds rectangles are preserved. Hytale requires extents matching cube face dimensions, swapped for 90/270-degree rotation; offsets and mirroring are supported.

rotation.description: UV rotation in degrees; nonzero rotation requires format uv_rotation support.

texture.description: Texture UUID, ID or unique name; false unassigns, null disables the face. Omit to preserve.

faces.description: Patch only these faces in per-face UV mode. Other faces are preserved. Explicit rectangles disable automatic UV remapping except in Hytale, where dimension-linked UVs retain native Auto UV. Hytale textures resolve through the project/attachment collection, so only null is accepted as an explicit face texture.

tools.name: remove_element
tools.title: Remove Element
tools.description: Removes the element with the given ID.

id.description: ID or name of the element to remove.

tools.name: add_group
tools.title: Add Group
tools.description: Adds a new group with the given name and options.

origin.description: Pivot point of the group as [x, y, z].

rotation.description: Rotation of the group in degrees as [x, y, z].

parent.description: Parent group UUID or name, or root for the project root.

autouv.description: Auto UV setting. 0 = disabled, 1 = enabled, 2 = relative auto UV.

shade.description: Outliner shading toggle, matching Blockbench's default (true). Ignored by Java 26.3+ projects, which use per-cube shade_direction_override instead.

tools.name: list_outline
tools.title: List Outline
tools.description: Returns the project outline as a hierarchical tree. Each node reports { name, uuid, type, children? }, including groups, armatures, armature bones, cubes, meshes and markers. Parent nodes retain their descendants. Use include_cubes=false and include_meshes=false to omit geometry leaves, or max_depth to bound very deep trees.

include_cubes.description: If true, include cubes as leaves. If false, omit cubes while retaining other node types.

include_meshes.description: If true, include meshes as leaves. If false, omit meshes.

max_depth.description: Maximum tree depth to traverse. Use a small value to summarize large projects.

tools.name: duplicate_element
tools.title: Duplicate Element
tools.description: Duplicates any outliner element or group (with its children) by ID or name using Blockbench's native duplicate, so every property, face UV, texture and mesh vertex key is preserved. Mesh copies inherit their armature bone vertex weights, and copied IK null objects point at the copied bones when their chain was duplicated with them. Optionally offsets the copy and assigns a new name. Selection is left unchanged.

id.description: ID or name of the element to duplicate.

offset.description: Model-space offset [x, y, z] applied to the copy and every descendant.

newName.description: Name for the top-level copy. Defaults to Blockbench's duplicate naming (trailing number incremented, unique where required).

tools.name: rename_element
tools.title: Rename Element
tools.description: Renames a cube, mesh or group by ID or name.

id.description: ID or name of the element to rename.

tools.name: find_elements_by_criteria
tools.title: Find Elements by Criteria
tools.description: Searches the current project for elements matching the given criteria. Supports name pattern matching (regex or substring), type filtering, scoping to a parent group, cube size ranges, and selection scope. Returns element metadata, never modifies state.

name_pattern.description: Regex pattern to match element names (e.g., '^arm_.*'). Case-sensitive. Patterns over 512 characters, with nested quantifiers such as (a+)+, or that do not compile are rejected with an error.

name_contains.description: Substring to match in element names. Case-insensitive.

type.description: Restrict to a single element type.

parent_group.description: UUID or name of a parent group. Only descendants of this group are returned.

min_size.description: Minimum [x,y,z] size for cubes. Cubes smaller on any axis are excluded.

max_size.description: Maximum [x,y,z] size for cubes. Cubes larger on any axis are excluded.

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return.

tools.name: select_all_of_type
tools.title: Select All of Type
tools.description: Selects all elements of the given type (cube, mesh, or group) in the current project. Optionally restrict to descendants of a parent group, or add to (rather than replace) the current selection. As in Blockbench, locked nodes are skipped and selecting a group also selects its contents.

add_to_selection.description: If true, add to current selection. If false, replace selection.

parent_group.description: UUID or name of a parent group. If provided, only descendants of this group are selected.

tools.name: filter_by_material
tools.title: Filter Elements by Material
tools.description: Returns all elements that reference the given texture. For cubes, includes the list of face keys (e.g., 'north', 'up') that use the texture. For meshes, returns the mesh if any face uses the texture.

texture.description: Texture ID, UUID or name to search for.

include_face_keys.description: Include the list of cube face keys (e.g., 'north') that reference the texture.

tools.name: get_selection
tools.title: Get Selection
tools.description: Returns the current selection state: selected cube/mesh/group UUIDs and names, plus the active texture. Use this to verify what `apply_texture` or a paint tool with `fill_mode="selected_elements"` will target.

tools.name: list_export_formats
tools.title: List Export Formats
tools.description: Lists registered export codecs, file extensions, compile/export support, and availability under the native export action's condition. Use before `export_model` to pick a codec.

only_current_format.description: If true, only return codecs compatible with the current project's format.

tools.name: export_model
tools.title: Export Model
tools.description: Compiles the current project through a codec whose native export action is available. Returns JSON metadata and a live .bbmodel resource link; result_format='embedded' returns complete exports as text/blob resources with URI and MIME type. Optionally writes to a local path (requires Blockbench filesystem permission). Partial codec options merge over the configured defaults; for glTF armatures, options.merge_armature=true merges each armature's meshes into one SkinnedMesh. Use `list_export_formats` to discover codecs.

codec_id.description: Codec ID to use for export (e.g., 'obj', 'gltf', 'project', 'bedrock'). If omitted, uses the current project format's codec. Use `list_export_formats` to see available IDs.

options.description: Codec-specific export options, merged over the codec's configured export options (keys match the native export dialog). glTF ('gltf'): encoding ('ascii' | 'binary'), scale, embed_textures, armature (export groups as skinned bones), animations, and merge_armature (Blockbench 5.2+; default false exports one SkinnedMesh per armature child mesh, true merges each armature's meshes into a single SkinnedMesh).

path.description: Absolute filesystem path to write the compiled model to. Requires user permission (Blockbench v5.0+ prompts for 'fs' access). If omitted, content is returned in the response only. Fails if the file exists unless overwrite is true.

overwrite.description: Replace an existing file at path. Defaults to false so an export never silently replaces another file.

max_content_length.description: Maximum characters of text or base64 to return. Use 0 to omit file content. In embedded mode, only complete files within this limit are embedded; larger files return a truncated preview in metadata.content.

result_format.description: text preserves the JSON metadata.content payload. embedded moves a complete file into an MCP resource block with URI and MIME type, sets metadata.content to null, and reports its resource_uri. Both modes include a link to the live .bbmodel project resource.

tools.name: get_undo_stack
tools.title: Get Undo Stack
tools.description: Returns the current undo/redo history: the list of edit entries, the current index, and which entries are undone vs. applied. Use this to inspect available undo/redo operations and find named checkpoints.

limit.description: Maximum number of entries to return (most recent first).

tools.name: save_checkpoint
tools.title: Save Checkpoint
tools.description: Inserts a named marker into the undo history. The marker can later be located with `get_undo_stack` so the agent knows how many times to call `undo` to return to this state. Does not modify the project.

name.description: Descriptive name for the checkpoint. Shown in undo history so agents can navigate back to this point.

tools.name: from_geo_json
tools.title: Import GeoJSON
tools.description: Imports one Bedrock geometry (.geo.json) into the current project, which keeps its format (one with bones: Bedrock, GeckoLib, generic, ...), as one undoable edit, and returns a screenshot. Adds the bones with their cubes, locators and texture meshes; the texture size, box UV mode and item display transforms it sets are undone with it, while the project's visible bounds can only grow. If the active project changes while loading, the import is rejected without modifying the new project. URLs on this computer or a private network are refused; pass a file path instead.

geojson.description: Bedrock geometry (format 1.12 or later) as inline JSON, an absolute path or file:// URL of a file on this computer (read with Blockbench's file permission), or a public http(s) URL (at most 10 MB).

geometry.description: Identifier of the geometry to import, such as geometry.robot, when the file holds several. Omit it when the file holds one.

tools.name: knife_cut_cube
tools.title: Knife Cut Cube
tools.description: Headless Blockbench Knife tool for cubes: splits each target cube with planes perpendicular to one axis at the given positions, keeping each piece's share of the face UVs. The original cube keeps the lowest piece; new pieces get unique names. One undo entry covers every cut and the selection is left unchanged.

cubes.description: Cube UUIDs or unique names to cut. Defaults to the selected cubes.

axis.description: Axis the cut plane is perpendicular to.

positions.description: Cut-plane coordinates along the axis, in the cube's from/to space (model space for unrotated cubes). Positions closer than the cube's inflate to its from/to edges, or outside it, are skipped for that cube and reported sorted and deduplicated.

tools.name: slice_cubes_to_block_grid
tools.title: Slice Cubes To Block Grid
tools.description: Cuts cubes wherever they cross a Bedrock block boundary (16-unit grid, x/z centered) and, by default, regroups the pieces into one group per block cell pivoted at that block's origin. Use it to divide an oversized custom block model into per-block sections that each fit Bedrock's 30×30×30 limit. Rotated cubes are left uncut on the affected axes and reported.

cubes.description: Cube UUIDs or unique names to slice. Defaults to every cube in the project.

axes.description: Axes to slice along. Cubes rotated (or inside groups rotated) about the other two axes are skipped on that axis, as Blockbench's own slicer does.

cell_size.description: Block size in model units; 16 for Bedrock. Horizontal boundaries sit at ±half a cell, vertical ones at multiples.

regroup.description: Move every resulting cube into a group named after its block cell (bottom, top, right_top_front, top2, …) pivoted at that block's origin, so each group is one exportable block section. Pieces leave their previous bone; the report lists each source cube's former group.

parent.description: Parent group UUID or name for the cell groups; must not be rotated. Defaults to the project root.

group_prefix.description: Prefix for cell group names, e.g. `goal_` yields `goal_top`. Existing groups are reused only when their name and block-origin pivot match; otherwise a numbered name is chosen.

tools.name: inspect_block_bounds
tools.title: Inspect Block Bounds
tools.description: Reports cube, group, and whole-model extents against Blockbench's Bedrock block limit (a 30×30×30 box whose center may sit up to 7 units from the block center), the block cell each cube occupies, and the grid cut positions slice_cubes_to_block_grid would use. Read-only. Extents ignore rotation; rotated cubes are flagged.

cubes.description: Cube UUIDs or unique names to inspect. Defaults to every cube in the project.

cell_size.description: Block size in model units; 16 for Bedrock.

max_size.description: Maximum geometry size per axis for one block (Bedrock: 30).

max_center_offset.description: How far the limit box may shift from the block center per axis (Bedrock: 7, giving x/z within ±22 and y within -14…30).

tools.name: flip_in_place
tools.title: Flip In Place
tools.description: Mirrors elements in place along an axis using Blockbench's native Flip In Place (flip_in_place_x/y/z): cubes flip around their own center, meshes around their origin, groups also invert rotations in bone-rig formats. For meshes in vertex/edge/face selection mode only the selected components flip. Edit mode only.

ids.description: Element or group UUIDs/names to flip. Replaces the selection with these. Defaults to the current selection.

axis.description: Axis to mirror across each element's own center (cubes) or pivot (meshes, groups, other elements).

tools.name: list_modes
tools.title: List Modes
tools.description: Lists Blockbench editor tabs/modes with IDs, names, native availability, and the current mode. Includes plugin-added modes. Use before set_mode to discover whether Edit, Paint, Animate, or Display is available for the current project. Camera angles are controlled separately by set_camera_angle.

tools.name: set_mode
tools.title: Set Mode
tools.description: Switches Blockbench's editor tab through its native mode trigger, respecting the mode's condition. Use mode_id='animate' to enter Animate before animation work, 'paint' before native painting tools, or 'edit' to return. Returns the resulting mode and available modes; refresh tools/list for changed tool availability. Selecting the current mode does nothing. Does not change the project's format. When the user enabled the AI Scratchpad setting, mode_id='ai_scratchpad' relaxes the format's cube size, rotation and integer-size guardrails until another mode is selected.

mode_id.description: Mode ID returned by list_modes, such as 'edit', 'paint', 'animate', or 'display'. The Animate tab uses 'animate'. The current project must satisfy the mode's native condition.

tools.name: paint_settings
tools.title: Paint Settings
tools.description: Configures paint mode settings and preferences, including Blockbench 5.2 screen-space brush projection, brush lock mode and brush aspect ratio. The result also reports the active opacity range (0-255 or 0-100); tool opacity parameters stay 0-255 and are converted automatically.

x.description: X coordinate of texture mirror center.

y.description: Y coordinate of texture mirror center.

paint_side_restrict.description: Restrict painting to current face side.

paint_with_stylus_only.description: Only allow painting with stylus input.

pick_color_opacity.description: Pick opacity when using color picker.

screen_space_brush_projection.description: Project brushes in screen space when painting in the 3D viewport (Blockbench 5.2+, brush tools only).

brush_lock_mode.description: Restrict viewport strokes: 'none', the 'element' the stroke started on, 'selected_faces', or the single 'face' it started on (Blockbench 5.2+).

brush_aspect_ratio.description: Brush aspect ratio (-16 to 16) applied to every tool that supports it (brush and copy brush; Blockbench 5.2+).

tools.name: create_brush_preset
tools.title: Create Brush Preset
tools.description: Creates a custom brush preset with specified settings. Omitted settings are stored as unset so loading the preset keeps the current value.

opacity.description: Opacity (0-255), independent of Blockbench's opacity range setting.

shape.description: Brush shape. Omit to keep the current shape when loading.

blend_mode.description: Brush blend mode. Omit to keep the current blend mode when loading.

screen_space.description: Enable screen-space brush projection when the preset is loaded (Blockbench 5.2+). Omit to keep the current setting.

tools.name: load_brush_preset
tools.title: Load Brush Preset
tools.description: Loads and applies a custom or built-in brush preset (e.g. 'screen_space') by name.

preset_name.description: Name of the brush preset to load: a custom preset name, or a built-in one such as 'pixel_brush', 'pixel_perfect', 'smooth_brush' or 'screen_space' (also accepts the full 'menu.brush_presets.*' key or its translated label).

tools.name: list_particle_presets
tools.title: List Particle Presets
tools.description: Lists particle effect presets (smoke, fire, sparks, magic, glow, snow, drip, ...), built-in sprites and textures, materials and facing modes. Every preset uses a texture that ships with Minecraft and Blockbench, so it previews and runs with no image file. Read this before create_particle_effect.

include_designs.description: Include each preset's design knobs, useful as a template for custom effects.

tools.name: create_particle_effect
tools.title: Create Particle Effect
tools.description: Creates a Bedrock particle effect (the Snowstorm format Blockbench, Minecraft Bedrock and GeckoLib use) from a preset plus design knobs, or from raw JSON. Writes <pack_root>/particles/<name>.json (and an optional custom texture to textures/particle/), validates it, and loads it into Blockbench's particle preview. Then place it with manage_particle_keyframes, usually at a locator from add_locator. Refuses invalid effects and existing files unless overwrite is true. Blockbench desktop only.

identifier.description: Particle identifier, lowercase namespace:name (for example mymod:chimney_smoke). Do not use the minecraft namespace for new effects.

preset.description: Starting point; list_particle_presets describes each. design knobs override it.

material.description: particles_alpha: cutout, cheapest. particles_blend: soft translucency (smoke, glow). particles_add: additive light (fire, magic, sparks). particles_opaque: solid.

sprite.description: Built-in sprite; sets the texture and UVs. See list_particle_presets for descriptions.

texture.description: Custom Bedrock texture path without .png, such as textures/particle/leaf. Overrides sprite.

texture_size.description: Pixel size of the custom texture. Tools fill it from the PNG when they copy one.

frame_size.description: Pixel width and height of one frame.

axis.description: Direction frames are stacked in the image; Blockbench flipbook textures are vertical.

fps.description: Playback rate. Omit to stretch the frames over each particle's lifetime.

loop.description: Loop the frames when fps is set.

flipbook.description: Animate a custom texture as a sprite sheet.

rate.description: Steady emission, particles per second. Mutually exclusive with burst.

burst.description: Emit this many particles at once when the emitter starts. Mutually exclusive with rate.

max_particles.description: Cap on live particles for a steady emitter.

looping.description: Emitter restarts after duration (+ sleep_time). An existing effect keeps its mode; a new one loops for rate and runs once for burst. Emitters fired from animation keyframes should not loop in Bedrock.

duration.description: Seconds the emitter is active per cycle. Loops default to 10: with no sleep_time the game emits continuously either way, and Blockbench's preview restarts a looping emitter every `duration` seconds, so keep it at least as long as the clip.

sleep_time.description: Pause between looping cycles, in seconds.

type.description: point: one spot. sphere/disc: radius around the emitter. box: half_dimensions. entity_aabb: the entity's hitbox (in-game only; Blockbench previews it as a point).

offset.description: Spawn center offset from the emitter, in blocks.

radius.description: Sphere or disc radius in blocks.

plane_normal.description: Disc facing; y (the default) lays it flat.

surface_only.description: Spawn on the surface/rim instead of throughout the volume.

direction.description: Initial direction: away from or toward the shape center, or a vector such as [0, 1, 0] (up). Molang allowed, e.g. ['math.random(-0.2,0.2)', 1, 0].

local_space.description: Particles move with the emitter (auras, rings on a moving bone). False leaves them behind (smoke, trails).

lifetime.description: Particle lifetime in seconds; [min, max] picks a random value per particle.

speed.description: Initial speed in blocks per second; [min, max] randomizes it.

acceleration.description: Blocks per second squared, e.g. [0, -9.8, 0] for gravity or [0, 0.5, 0] for rising smoke.

drag.description: Linear drag coefficient; 1-3 slows bursts naturally.

size.description: Billboard half-width in blocks (Bedrock sizes are half extents: 0.5 spans a whole block), or [start, end] to grow or shrink over life. Vanilla smoke is 0.1.

size_variation.description: Random size spread per particle, 0-1 (0.3 means +/-15%).

spin.description: Billboard rotation in degrees and degrees per second.

color.description: Tint as #RRGGBB/#RRGGBBAA, or 2-8 colors spread evenly over the particle's life. White keeps a sprite's own colors.

fade_out.description: true fades alpha to zero at the end of life; false makes the end opaque again. Without color it adjusts the current tint. Needs particles_blend or particles_add to look smooth.

facing.description: Billboard orientation. lookat_xyz faces the camera; lookat_y stays upright; direction_* and lookat_direction stretch along velocity (sparks, rain).

lighting.description: Shade the particle by world light. Leave off for glowing effects.

radius.description: Collision radius in blocks (Bedrock allows up to 0.5).

bounciness.description: Coefficient of restitution; 0 stops dead, 0.5 bounces.

expire_on_contact.description: Remove the particle when it hits a block (drips, rain).

collision.description: Collide with world blocks. Blockbench's preview has no blocks, so collisions only show in game.

components.description: Raw Bedrock components merged over the built effect, keyed like minecraft:particle_motion_dynamic. Objects merge; null deletes a component or field. Use for anything the knobs do not cover.

curves.description: Raw Bedrock curves (variable.<name> keys), merged over the built effect.

events.description: Raw Bedrock events, merged over the built effect.

design.description: Knobs layered over the preset (or over a plain default effect). Units are blocks (16 model units) and seconds.

raw.description: A complete Bedrock particle file (for example a Snowstorm export) instead of preset/design. Its identifier is replaced by `identifier`.

texture.description: Blockbench texture UUID or name to save as the particle texture (paint or generate it first).

path.description: Absolute path to a PNG file to copy.

name.description: File name under textures/particle/; defaults to the effect name.

texture_image.description: Custom texture for the effect. It is saved to <pack_root>/textures/particle/<name>.png and the effect's texture and texture_size are set from it (keep design.sprite unset).

pack_root.description: Absolute resource-pack-style folder that receives particles/<name>.json and textures/particle/*.png. Defaults to the pack of a Bedrock entity opened from a resource pack, else the saved project's folder.

overwrite.description: Replace an existing effect file (and texture) with the same name.

tools.name: update_particle_effect
tools.title: Update Particle Effect
tools.description: Changes an existing particle effect file with design knobs (only the components each knob owns are rewritten) or replaces it with raw JSON, validates it, saves it and refreshes the preview. Also loads an effect file from disk that Blockbench has not seen yet. Blockbench desktop only.

effect.description: Particle identifier (mymod:smoke), effect name (smoke), or absolute path to the effect's .json file. A path that is not loaded yet is loaded.

material.description: particles_alpha: cutout, cheapest. particles_blend: soft translucency (smoke, glow). particles_add: additive light (fire, magic, sparks). particles_opaque: solid.

sprite.description: Built-in sprite; sets the texture and UVs. See list_particle_presets for descriptions.

texture.description: Custom Bedrock texture path without .png, such as textures/particle/leaf. Overrides sprite.

texture_size.description: Pixel size of the custom texture. Tools fill it from the PNG when they copy one.

frame_size.description: Pixel width and height of one frame.

axis.description: Direction frames are stacked in the image; Blockbench flipbook textures are vertical.

fps.description: Playback rate. Omit to stretch the frames over each particle's lifetime.

loop.description: Loop the frames when fps is set.

flipbook.description: Animate a custom texture as a sprite sheet.

rate.description: Steady emission, particles per second. Mutually exclusive with burst.

burst.description: Emit this many particles at once when the emitter starts. Mutually exclusive with rate.

max_particles.description: Cap on live particles for a steady emitter.

looping.description: Emitter restarts after duration (+ sleep_time). An existing effect keeps its mode; a new one loops for rate and runs once for burst. Emitters fired from animation keyframes should not loop in Bedrock.

duration.description: Seconds the emitter is active per cycle. Loops default to 10: with no sleep_time the game emits continuously either way, and Blockbench's preview restarts a looping emitter every `duration` seconds, so keep it at least as long as the clip.

sleep_time.description: Pause between looping cycles, in seconds.

type.description: point: one spot. sphere/disc: radius around the emitter. box: half_dimensions. entity_aabb: the entity's hitbox (in-game only; Blockbench previews it as a point).

offset.description: Spawn center offset from the emitter, in blocks.

radius.description: Sphere or disc radius in blocks.

plane_normal.description: Disc facing; y (the default) lays it flat.

surface_only.description: Spawn on the surface/rim instead of throughout the volume.

direction.description: Initial direction: away from or toward the shape center, or a vector such as [0, 1, 0] (up). Molang allowed, e.g. ['math.random(-0.2,0.2)', 1, 0].

local_space.description: Particles move with the emitter (auras, rings on a moving bone). False leaves them behind (smoke, trails).

lifetime.description: Particle lifetime in seconds; [min, max] picks a random value per particle.

speed.description: Initial speed in blocks per second; [min, max] randomizes it.

acceleration.description: Blocks per second squared, e.g. [0, -9.8, 0] for gravity or [0, 0.5, 0] for rising smoke.

drag.description: Linear drag coefficient; 1-3 slows bursts naturally.

size.description: Billboard half-width in blocks (Bedrock sizes are half extents: 0.5 spans a whole block), or [start, end] to grow or shrink over life. Vanilla smoke is 0.1.

size_variation.description: Random size spread per particle, 0-1 (0.3 means +/-15%).

spin.description: Billboard rotation in degrees and degrees per second.

color.description: Tint as #RRGGBB/#RRGGBBAA, or 2-8 colors spread evenly over the particle's life. White keeps a sprite's own colors.

fade_out.description: true fades alpha to zero at the end of life; false makes the end opaque again. Without color it adjusts the current tint. Needs particles_blend or particles_add to look smooth.

facing.description: Billboard orientation. lookat_xyz faces the camera; lookat_y stays upright; direction_* and lookat_direction stretch along velocity (sparks, rain).

lighting.description: Shade the particle by world light. Leave off for glowing effects.

radius.description: Collision radius in blocks (Bedrock allows up to 0.5).

bounciness.description: Coefficient of restitution; 0 stops dead, 0.5 bounces.

expire_on_contact.description: Remove the particle when it hits a block (drips, rain).

collision.description: Collide with world blocks. Blockbench's preview has no blocks, so collisions only show in game.

components.description: Raw Bedrock components merged over the built effect, keyed like minecraft:particle_motion_dynamic. Objects merge; null deletes a component or field. Use for anything the knobs do not cover.

curves.description: Raw Bedrock curves (variable.<name> keys), merged over the built effect.

events.description: Raw Bedrock events, merged over the built effect.

design.description: Knobs to change. Only the components a knob owns are rewritten; hand-written parts of the file stay.

raw.description: Replace the whole file with this Bedrock particle JSON. The effect keeps its current identifier, so keyframes and the client entity still match.

texture.description: Blockbench texture UUID or name to save as the particle texture (paint or generate it first).

path.description: Absolute path to a PNG file to copy.

name.description: File name under textures/particle/; defaults to the effect name.

texture_image.description: Custom texture for the effect. It is saved to <pack_root>/textures/particle/<name>.png and the effect's texture and texture_size are set from it (keep design.sprite unset).

overwrite.description: Replace a texture PNG that already exists with different content (another effect may use it).

tools.name: list_particle_effects
tools.title: List Particle Effects
tools.description: Lists particle effects loaded in Blockbench with their file, summary, texture status and validation warnings, every particle keyframe that uses them, keyframes that have no preview file or point at missing locators, and the client-entity particle_effects map a Bedrock pack needs.

tools.name: manage_particle_keyframes
tools.title: Manage Particle Keyframes
tools.description: Adds, removes or lists particle keyframes on an animation's Effects track. A keyframe spawns an effect at a time, optionally at a locator; Blockbench previews it in Animate mode (set_mode animate, then animation_timeline set_time and capture a screenshot). Keyframes export with Bedrock and GeckoLib animations. One undo step.

animation_id.description: Animation UUID or name. If not provided, uses current animation.

action.description: add particle keyframes, remove them by time, or list them.

time.description: Seconds from the start of the animation.

effect.description: Effect to spawn: identifier, effect name or JSON path of a loaded effect. For GeckoLib, a name your mod's particle handler understands also works (without a preview).

effect_name.description: Name written to the keyframe and used in the client entity's particle_effects map; defaults to the effect's short name.

locator.description: Locator the effect spawns at and follows. Omit to spawn at the entity origin.

pre_effect_script.description: Molang run before the emitter starts, for variables such as variable.color = 1;

bind_to_actor.description: Bedrock: keep the emitter attached to the entity. False leaves it in the world where it spawned.

keyframes.description: Keyframes for add. A keyframe at an existing particle time joins that keyframe as another effect.

times.description: Times (seconds) to remove for remove; omit to remove every particle keyframe.

effect_filter.description: For remove: only effects with this name, identifier or file.

tools.name: export_particle_pack
tools.title: Export Particle Pack
tools.description: Delivers particle effects to a Bedrock resource pack: writes particles/<name>.json and copies custom textures to textures/particle/, then returns the particle_effects map to paste into the client entity so animation keyframe names resolve. Defaults to every effect the project's keyframes use. Skips identical files; refuses to overwrite different ones unless overwrite is true. Blockbench desktop only.

destination.description: Absolute path to the resource pack root (the folder containing manifest.json).

items.description: Particle identifier (mymod:smoke), effect name (smoke), or absolute path to the effect's .json file. A path that is not loaded yet is loaded.

effects.description: Effects to deliver. Defaults to every effect used by particle keyframes in the project.

overwrite.description: Replace files that exist with different content. Identical files are always skipped.

tools.name: get_average_fps
tools.title: Get Average FPS
tools.description: Measures the average frames per second of Blockbench's render loop by counting rendered frames for duration_ms, then returns the average with the frame count, the fps_limit setting, Blockbench's own last-second counter, window focus at the start of the window plus whether it changed, whether the page was hidden, and whether rendering was paused. The call waits for the whole window; keep other tools idle meanwhile for a representative reading. A minimised or fully occluded Blockbench renders no frames and freezes its timers, so the call returns an empty window at once with document_hidden and rendering_paused set rather than waiting; bring the window to the foreground to measure a real frame rate.

duration_ms.description: Sampling window in milliseconds (250–10000). The call waits this long while counting rendered frames.

tools.name: create_project
tools.title: Create Project
tools.description: Creates a project with the given name and format, and returns a resource link to its live .bbmodel file.

format.description: Project format ID from Blockbench's Formats registry (e.g. bedrock_block, java_block, free). Unknown IDs are rejected with the list of valid IDs.

tools.name: get_project_info
tools.title: Get Project Info
tools.description: Returns read-only project orientation: format id and display name, project name/UUID, texture resolution (texture_width/height), element counts, and a summary of top-level groups. Includes structured JSON and a resource link to the live .bbmodel project file. Prefer this over `risky_eval` for first-look inspection.

tools.name: create_texture
tools.title: Create Texture
tools.description: Creates a new texture with the given name and size.

uv_width.description: Logical UV width for formats with per_texture_uv_size. Supply uv_height too. Independent of bitmap width; omit both to preserve native defaults.

uv_height.description: Logical UV height for formats with per_texture_uv_size. Supply uv_width too. Independent of bitmap height.

data.description: Image data URL, or an absolute path or file:// URL of an image file (desktop only, read with Blockbench's file permission).

fill_color.description: RGBA color to fill the texture, as tuple or HEX string.

layer_name.description: Deprecated and ignored: textures are created without layers. Use texture_layer_management create_layer to add a named layer.

pbr_channel.description: PBR channel to use for the texture. Color, normal, height, or Metalness/Emissive/Roughness (MER) map.

render_mode.description: Render mode for the texture. Default, emissive, additive, or layered.

render_sides.description: Render sides for the texture. Auto, front, or double.

tools.name: add_texture_group
tools.title: Add Texture Group
tools.description: Adds a reversible texture group. All texture references must exist. Material groups require one texture per channel, either normal or height, and a color map alongside a MER map; use is_material=false for ordinary grouping.

textures.description: Array of texture IDs or names to add to the group.

is_material.description: Whether the texture group is a PBR material or not.

tools.name: list_textures
tools.title: List Textures
tools.description: Returns a list of all textures in the Blockbench editor.

tools.name: create_pbr_material
tools.title: Create PBR Material
tools.description: Creates a new PBR material (texture group with is_material=true) and optionally assigns textures to PBR channels. Requires a PBR-capable format, distinct textures per channel, either normal or height, and a color texture alongside a MER texture. Uniform values require the corresponding map to be absent. Creation and texture moves are one undoable edit.

color_texture.description: Texture ID/name for the color (albedo) channel.

normal_texture.description: Texture ID/name for the normal map channel.

height_texture.description: Texture ID/name for the height/displacement map channel.

mer_texture.description: Texture ID/name for the MER (Metalness/Emissive/Roughness) channel.

color_value.description: Uniform RGBA color [R,G,B,A] when no color texture is provided.

mer_value.description: Uniform MER values [Metalness, Emissive, Roughness] (0-255) when no MER texture is provided.

subsurface_value.description: Subsurface scattering value (0-255) for Bedrock 1.21.30+ materials.

tools.name: configure_material
tools.title: Configure Material
tools.description: Configures a PBR material in one undoable edit. Replaced maps are detached without deleting their textures. Use 'none' to clear a channel before using uniform values or switching between normal and height; a MER map requires a color map.

material.description: Material name or UUID to configure.

color_texture.description: Texture ID/name for the color channel, or 'none' to use uniform color.

normal_texture.description: Texture ID/name for the normal map, or 'none' to remove.

height_texture.description: Texture ID/name for the height map, or 'none' to remove.

mer_texture.description: Texture ID/name for MER channel, or 'none' to use uniform values.

color_value.description: Uniform RGBA color [R,G,B,A] when no color texture.

tools.name: list_materials
tools.title: List Materials
tools.description: Lists all PBR materials (texture groups with is_material=true) and their assigned textures per channel.

tools.name: get_material_info
tools.title: Get Material Info
tools.description: Gets detailed information about a PBR material including the compiled texture_set.json preview for Bedrock export.

tools.name: import_texture_set
tools.title: Import Texture Set
tools.description: Imports a Minecraft Bedrock texture_set.json on desktop. Validates supported JSON and decodes referenced images before one undoable edit. Returns JSON with material name/UUID and path. Reuses already loaded image paths without deleting textures. Normal and height, or MER and MERS, cannot coexist; MER images require a color image.

path.description: Path to the .texture_set.json file to import.

tools.name: assign_texture_channel
tools.title: Assign Texture Channel
tools.description: Assigns a texture to one PBR channel in a single undoable edit. Detaches the previous map without deleting it or changing its channel. Normal and height cannot coexist; a MER map requires a color map, including in the source material after moving textures.

texture.description: Texture name or UUID to assign.

channel.description: PBR channel to assign the texture to.

tools.name: save_material_config
tools.title: Save Material Config
tools.description: Saves the material's texture_set.json file to disk (Bedrock format). Requires the color texture to have a valid file path.

material.description: Material name or UUID to save.

tools.name: trigger_action
tools.title: Trigger Action
tools.description: Triggers an available Blockbench Action and respects its condition. The native action owns Undo; only a newly opened dialog may be auto-confirmed.

action.description: Action ID from Blockbench's BarItems registry.

confirmDialog.description: Whether to confirm a newly opened dialog from this action. Existing unrelated dialogs are never confirmed.

confirmEvent.description: JSON object of MouseEvent options, with optional event type (default click).

tools.name: risky_eval
tools.title: Eval
tools.description: Evaluates JavaScript and returns its JSON result. Does not create an Undo entry. Mutating code must manage its own correctly scoped Undo transaction; read-only evaluation leaves history unchanged.

code.description: JavaScript code to evaluate. Do not pass `console` commands or comments.

tools.name: emulate_clicks
tools.title: Emulate Clicks
tools.description: Emulates clicks on the given interface elements.

duration.description: Duration of the drag in milliseconds.

drag.description: Drag options. If set, will perform a drag from position to 'to'.

tools.name: geckolib_list_easings
tools.title: List GeckoLib Easings
tools.description: Lists every easing name GeckoLib accepts on keyframes, which of them read easingArgs, and each argument's default and meaning. Needs no project, so it can be called while planning an animation.
